whatIs.title: What is Mediation?
whatIs.desc1: Mediation is an alternative dispute resolution method where a neutral third party (mediator) helps disputing parties find a mutually acceptable solution.
whatIs.desc2: In mediation, the mediator does not make decisions but guides parties towards dialogue and helps identify their interests.
whatIs.neutralDesc: The mediator does not side with either party and maintains a neutral position

benefits.title: Benefits of Mediation
benefits.subtitle: Why mediation can be more effective than court proceedings?

speed.title: Speed
speed.desc: The mediation process usually takes from a few days to a few weeks, whereas court proceedings can last for months.

cost.title: Cost-effective
cost.desc: Mediation costs are significantly lower than court fees. You save time and money.

privacy.title: Confidentiality
privacy.desc: Unlike court proceedings, mediation is confidential. Your case will not become public.

relations.title: Preserving Relationships
relations.desc: Mediation helps preserve relationships between parties.

control.title: Control
control.desc: Parties have full control over the process and outcome. The decision is made by them.

flexibility.title: Flexibility
flexibility.desc: The mediation process can be adapted to the needs of the parties.

process.title: Mediation Process
process.subtitle: Mediation is carried out in 4 stages

steps.title: Preliminary Consultation
steps.desc: Separate discussion with parties and explanation of the mediation process.

steps.title: Joint Session
steps.desc: Bringing parties together and discussing the problem.

steps.title: Negotiations
steps.desc: Identifying parties' interests and searching for solution options.

steps.title: Agreement
steps.desc: Reaching a mutually acceptable solution and drafting the agreement document.
